wait_time: minutes to a few days depending on size
format: .zip containing JSON or HTML files and media

request.label: Meta Accounts Center - Download your information

steps.title: Open Download your information
steps.detail: Go to Accounts Center, then Your information and permissions, then Download your information. Sign in if asked.

steps.title: Choose the Facebook profile
steps.detail: If your accounts are linked, select the Facebook profile whose data you want.

steps.title: Select information and range
steps.detail: Set the date range to All time unless you have a reason not to. Meta defaults to a recent window on some screens, and a range quietly left at twelve months produces an export that looks complete and is missing most of your life. Tick everything you care about; posts, photos and messages are separate selections.

steps.title: Pick format and quality
steps.detail: Choose JSON for the format. For media quality, High keeps your photographs at full size and roughly doubles the archive - often past 12 GB for a long-standing account - while Medium is far smaller and permanently smaller in quality. If this export is the copy you intend to keep, choose High: it is the only chance to get the originals out.

steps.title: Create the file and wait
steps.detail: Submit the request. Meta prepares the download and notifies you when it is ready.

steps.title: Download the file
steps.detail: The link is emailed and expires in a few days, so download it promptly. Save every part if it arrives split, keep them in one folder, and do not unzip - Muletto reads the archives directly.

notes: Facebook and Instagram both live in Meta Accounts Center, so you can request them from the same place.
Choose JSON if you plan to search or organize the data - it is far cleaner to work with than the HTML version.
Meta produces this export for Facebook and Instagram separately, even when the accounts are linked. Request each one.
HTML exports cannot be read back by Muletto or by anything else. If you already have one, request JSON as well - it costs another wait and nothing else.
The wait is usually minutes to hours rather than days, but Meta gives no progress and the email is the only signal.

explain.title: JSON, not HTML, and it is not obvious why
explain.body: Meta offers both. HTML looks friendlier - it opens in a browser and resembles Facebook - but it is a rendering of your data rather than the data, and nothing can reliably read it back. JSON is the machine-readable one, and it is what Muletto reads. Pick HTML and you have a scrapbook you can only look at; pick JSON and you have your data, which Muletto turns into something you can look at anyway.
